SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section 2, Special Branch.
REPORT
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE S. B. REGISTRY File No. B.D. 6582）
Date November 7, 19 35.

Subject Tower Night Club: Licence and closing time.

Made by D.P.S. Henchman. Forwarded by （签名）

The Tower Night Club, situated on the 9th floor of
the Cathay Hotel, was established on 19th October 1935.
It is an integral part of the Cathay Hotel and is under the
same general management. F. Kauffman sub-manages the "club"
and acts in the capacity of receptionist. The licence which
covers the Cathay Ball Room, also covers the Tower Night
Club, both being under the same management, i.e. that of the
Cathay Hotel. It appears that in the case of both the
Ball Room and the Tower Night Club a breach of licence
conditions has occurred, in so much as both these dance
halls have been kept open until after 2 a.m. This breach
of regulations takes place on Sunday mornings when the
management have been in the habit of keeping open-house
until 4 a.m. To keep open until 4 a.m. an extension is
required. In the case of the Cathay Ball Room this extension
was in force until early last year when the manager, Mr. Carrard,
voluntarily applied to have it cancelled. When the new
manager, Mr. Suter, took over, he failed to apply for a
renewal of the extension and he states that he was unaware
that it had been previously cancelled. An extension in
favour of the Ball Room would also have covered the Tower
Night Club and Mr. Suter states that when the latter was
opened in October, he was still under the impression that the
old extension was valid.
Mr. Suter, when interviewed by the undersigned, admitted
his error and stated that the management were prepared to
apply at once for the necessary extension and to pay the
arrears due in respect of the occasions when both Ball Room
and "Club" had been kept open without the necessary permit.

D.C. (Sp.Br.).
（签名） Henchman D.P.S.

报告
（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处特务科登记处 档案号 B.D. 6582）
日期 1935年11月7日。

事由 塔楼夜总会：执照及打烊时间。

呈报人 副督察长 Henchman。转呈人 （签名）

位于华懋饭店九楼的塔楼夜总会（Tower Night Club）于1935年10月19日开业。
该夜总会是华懋饭店不可分割的一部分，由同一总管理处管理。F. Kauffman 担任该“俱乐部”的副经理，并履行接待员职责。涵盖华懋舞厅的执照同样涵盖塔楼夜总会，因为两者均由同一管理方，即华懋饭店管理。看来，华懋舞厅和塔楼夜总会均存在违反执照条件的情况，因为这两个舞厅都营业至凌晨2点以后。这种违规行为发生在周日清晨，管理层习惯于将场所开放至凌晨4点。若要营业至凌晨4点，则需申请延期许可。就华懋舞厅而言，该延期许可有效期至去年年初，当时经理 Carrard 先生自愿申请取消该许可。当新经理 Suter 先生接任时，他未能申请续期该延期许可，并称其不知晓该许可此前已被取消。针对舞厅的延期许可本也可涵盖塔楼夜总会，Suter 先生称，在该夜总会于10月开业时，他仍以为旧的延期许可有效。
Suter 先生在接受卑职问询时承认了其错误，并表示管理层准备立即申请必要的延期许可，并支付在舞厅和“俱乐部”无必要许可证期间营业所欠的费用。

D.C. (特务科)。
（签名） 副督察长 Henchman

Date 193

situated at Road. Period
for
CONDITIONS.
1. That the licence be not transferable.
2. That the licence number plate be fixed in a conspicuous position at the main outside entrance to the premises and remain at all times legible and undefaced and that the licence be exhibited in a conspicuous place inside the premises.
3. That free access be given to the officers of the Council charged with the inspection of licensed premises.
4. That the licensee carry out forthwith such alterations and additions to the licensed premises as may from time to time be considered requisite by the Council.
5. That no alteration or addition, structural or otherwise, be made to the licensed premises without a permit first obtained therefor.
6. That no meeting of a political nature or at which any address or discussion on politics is allowed, nor any meeting which may cause a breach of the peace and good order of the Settlement be permitted in or upon any part of the premises without the written sanction of the Council first had and obtained.
6a. That in the case of a dancing saloon or other place for public dancing no persons under 15 years of age (foreign reckoning) be employed on or permitted to visit the premises.
6b. That in the case of a dancing saloon or other place for public dancing the licensee supply to the Council, on the first day of each and every month, a list of professional dancers employed on the premises. Said list shall specify the name, age, sex, nationality and residence of every such professional dancer.
7. That no obscene or indecent performance and no performance liable to cause a breach of the peace or affect the good order of the Settlement take place.
8. That no drunkenness, noise, disorderly conduct, or gambling be permitted on the premises.
9. That no prize-fight or boxing competition be permitted in the premises.
10. That a good light be kept after dark over the principal door of the premises so long as they remain open.
11. That the premises be closed at 2 a.m. and not reopened until 6 a.m.
12. That approved arrangements be made and maintained to the satisfaction of the Council for the escape in case of fire or panic of all persons from any part of the premises.
13. That approved fire hydrants, pumping connexions, sprinklers, drenchers and other necessary fire appliances, of such numbers and quality as are required by the Council, and made to the Fire Brigade pattern and gauge, be provided on the premises, where required by the Council, and be always kept in good working order to the satisfaction of the Chief Officer of the Fire Brigade, and that the same be kept at all times free from obstruction and ready for use.
14. That if required by the Council a plan with full particulars of the position and construction of all stalls, side-shows, and seating arrangements be submitted for its approval.
15. That all doors and barriers open outwards and be kept open during the presence of the public be fastened by a hook against the wall, or if kept closed be fastened or fastened only with automatic bolts of a pattern to be approved by and maintained to the satisfaction of the Council.
16. That all exit doors and other doors as openings which may be used by the public for the purpose of exit be indicated as such by a fixed lighted transparency of an approved pattern bearing the word "Exit" in 6-in letters, and that all such doors be opened immediately before the close of any performance, and where required by the Council such "Exit" signs shall be in both English and Chinese.
17. That all gangways, passages and staircases intended for the use of the audience be kept entirely free from chairs or any other obstructions, whether permanent or temporary, and that no person be permitted to stand therein.
18. That a notice be painted on all exit doors clearly indicating the method of opening them, and where required by the Council such notices shall be in both English and Chinese.
19. That all doors or openings which are in sight of the public in the premises but do not lead to exits be indicated by a fixed lighted transparency of an approved pattern bearing the words "No Exit" in 6-in. letters, and where required by the Council such words shall be in both English and Chinese.
20. That all "Exit" and "No Exit" lights and floor lights be kept lighted during the presence of the public.
21. That if required a duplicate system of lighting be installed and maintained to the satisfaction of the Council, and that the lights in every portion of the premises accessible to the public, other than the auditorium, be kept fully lighted during the presence of the public.
22. That the lighting, heating and ventilation be such as is approved by the Council and that no alteration or addition be made thereto without the approval of the Council.
23. That all curtains covering doors or hung in passages be so hung as not to trail on the ground.
24. That the use of corridors as cloak-rooms be not permitted and that no pegs for hats and cloaks be allowed therein.
25. That all scenery, wings, sky borders, draperies, floral decoration, properties, hangings, curtains, etc., whether on the stage, in the auditorium, or in other parts of the premises be rendered and maintained non-inflammable when required by the Council.
26. That smoking be not permitted on the premises should the Council so require.
27. That no accumulation of dirt, rubbish or inflammable material be permitted in any part of the premises.
28. That if required by the Council the premises be connected with the Central Fire Station by means of a telephone or fire alarm at the licensee's expense and that a report of any fire or alarm of fire, however slight, be at once sent to the Fire Station.
29. That when required by the Council there shall be a Municipal fireman or firemen on duty for whose services the usual fees shall be paid to the Council by the licensee.
30. That the premises be provided with proper sanitary conveniences.
31. That the premises be maintained in an approved sanitary condition and the business be conducted in accordance with the requirements of public health and to the satisfaction of the Commissioner of Public Health.
32. That no prizes or presents be given or lotteries held in connexion with the sale of tickets of admission by way of an inducement to the public to patronise the premises.
33. That no gratuity of any kind be offered or given to any employee of the Council.
34. That the licensee be solely and entirely responsible for any breach or disregard of any condition contained in this licence by himself, his servants, agents, tenants, lessees, or others.
35. That the General Municipal Rate payable in respect of the said premises be paid within fourteen days after the date on which it shall become due for payment.
36. That immediate notice be given to the Municipal Police of any death or crime occurring on the premises.
37. That not more than ............ persons, exclusive of those in the employ of the licensee be permitted to be in or upon the premises at any one time.
38. That on a breach of any of its conditions the licence be subject to withdrawal or suspension by the Council, and the whole or any part of the money deposited as security be liable to forfeiture at the option of the Council.

条件。
1. 本执照不得转让。
2. 执照号牌应固定在场所主要外部入口处的显眼位置，并始终保持清晰可辨且无污损，执照应在场所内部显眼处展示。
3. 应向负责检查持牌场所的工部局官员提供自由进入的便利。
4. 持证人应立即按照工部局不时认为必要的要求，对持牌场所进行改造和增建。
5. 未经事先获得许可，不得对持牌场所进行任何结构性或其他方面的改造或增建。
6. 未经工部局事先书面批准，不得在场所的任何部分允许举行具有政治性质的会议，或允许发表政治演说或进行政治讨论的会议，也不得允许任何可能导致破坏租界和平与良好秩序的会议。
6a. 若是舞厅或其他公共舞蹈场所，不得雇佣或允许未满15岁（按外国算法）的人员在场所内工作或访问。
6b. 若是舞厅或其他公共舞蹈场所，持证人应于每月第一天向工部局提交一份在场所内受雇的职业舞者名单。该名单应注明每位职业舞者的姓名、年龄、性别、国籍和住址。
7. 不得上演淫秽或不雅表演，也不得上演可能破坏和平或影响租界良好秩序的表演。
8. 场所内不得允许醉酒、噪音、扰乱秩序行为或赌博。
9. 场所内不得允许举行拳击比赛或拳击竞赛。
10. 天黑后，只要场所保持开放，正门上方应保持良好的照明。
11. 场所应于凌晨2点关闭，直至早上6点方可重新开放。
12. 应制定并维持经工部局满意的批准安排，以便在发生火灾或恐慌时，所有人员能从场所的任何部分逃生。
13. 应按工部局要求的数量和质量，提供经批准的消防栓、泵接合器、洒水器、喷淋器及其他必要的消防器材，并符合消防队规定的样式和规格；在工部局要求时，这些设备应安装在场所内，并始终保持良好工作状态，令消防总队队长满意；同时应始终保持这些设备无障碍物遮挡并随时可用。
14. 若工部局要求，应提交一份详细说明所有摊位、附属表演区及座位安排位置和构造的平面图，以供批准。
15. 所有门和屏障应向外开启，并在公众在场期间保持开启状态，用挂钩固定在墙上；若保持关闭，则仅能使用经工部局批准并令其满意的自动插销固定。
16. 所有出口门及其他可供公众用于出口的开口，应以固定的发光透明标志标示，标志采用经批准的样式，以6英寸字母标明“Exit”（出口）字样；所有此类门应在任何演出结束前立即打开；若工部局要求，此类“出口”标志应同时使用英文和中文。
17. 供观众使用的所有通道、走廊和楼梯应完全清除椅子或任何其他障碍物，无论是永久性的还是临时性的，并且不得允许任何人在其中站立。
18. 所有出口门上应漆有清晰指示开启方法的告示；若工部局要求，此类告示应同时使用英文和中文。
19. 场所内公众可见但不通向出口的所有门或开口，应以固定的发光透明标志标示，标志采用经批准的样式，以6英寸字母标明“No Exit”（非出口）字样；若工部局要求，此类字样应同时使用英文和中文。
20. 所有“出口”和“非出口”指示灯及地面灯在公众在场期间应保持点亮。
21. 若要求，应安装并维持令工部局满意的双重照明系统；在公众在场期间，除观众席外，场所内所有公众可进入的区域应保持充分照明。
22. 照明、供暖和通风设施应经工部局批准，未经工部局批准，不得对其进行任何改造或增建。
23. 覆盖门或悬挂在通道中的所有窗帘，其悬挂方式不得拖地。
24. 不得将走廊用作衣帽间，其中不得设置挂帽子和外套的挂钩。
25. 无论位于舞台、观众席还是场所其他部分的所有布景、侧幕、天幕、帷幔、花卉装饰、道具、悬挂物、窗帘等，在工部局要求时，应经过并保持阻燃处理。
26. 若工部局要求，场所内不得吸烟。
27. 场所任何部分不得堆积污垢、垃圾或易燃材料。
28. 若工部局要求，持证人应自费通过电话或火警报警器将场所与中央消防站连接，并立即向消防站报告任何火灾或火警，无论火势多么轻微。
29. 若工部局要求，应有市政消防员值班，持证人应向工部局支付其服务的常规费用。
30. 场所应配备适当的卫生设施。
31. 场所应保持经批准的卫生状况，经营活动应符合公共卫生要求并令公共卫生处处长满意。
32. 不得以奖品或礼物作为诱饵，或通过抽奖方式诱导公众光顾场所，以此促进门票销售。
33. 不得向工部局任何雇员提供或给予任何形式的酬金。
34. 持证人对其本人、其仆人、代理人、租户、承租人或其他人违反或忽视本执照所含任何条件的行为承担全部且唯一的责任。
35. 上述场所应付的一般市政捐税，应在到期应付之日起十四天内缴清。
36. 场所内发生任何死亡或犯罪案件，应立即通知市政警察。
37. 任何时候，场所内允许容纳的人数不得超过............人，不包括受雇于持证人的员工。
38. 若违反任何条件，工部局有权撤销或暂停本执照，并有权选择没收全部或部分作为保证金存入的款项。

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, MARCH 14, 1935
S. B. REGISTRY.
6-7-8
930—Berlin—Marlene Meets von Sternberg

Before January, 1930, the name of Marlene Dietrich was practically unknown. But one night at Fredy Kauffmann's Jockey Club the director and the star met for the first time, for at the Jockey Club those things always happened. The picture above was taken on the night of the meeting. At the left is Mr. Kauffmann, Director von Sternberg is hiding behind the paper horse, on the chair is Gustav Froelich, famous German film director, and at the right is fair Marlene. Mr. Kauffmann is now in Shanghai and hopes to start a "Jockey Club" here.

Maestro Of Berlin's Famous
Jockey Club Has Plans Here

Fredy Kauffmann, Newly Arrived, Sees Need Of
Real Night Club In Shanghai; Declares Night
Life Of City Is Boring, Dull, Insufferable

Boredom.
Insufferable, complete, sleazy, lazy, dull, dead, colorless, fatalistic boredom is the "feature" of Shanghai's nightlife, according to Mr. Fredy Kauffmann, late maestro of the famous Jockey Club of that center of nightlife, Berlin.

But according to Fredy (because he doesn't like to be called "Mister") Shanghailanders don't want to be bored. If they were to be given a real club, a real atmosphere, an atmosphere without the stodgy formality of contemporary nightlife, if they were once acquainted with real spontaneity, well—then things would be different. And Fredy is out to establish just that kind of club.

But who is Fredy? A white-haired, pleasant, middle-age German, friend of artists, actresses, celebrities, authors, everywhere. It all happened back in 1929, or really before them. Before then Fredy was a photographer, and an actor on both the stage and screen. But in 1929 he saw through the hollowness of Berlin night life. He started his own Club—The Jockey Club—and from the moment the doors first swung open it was a success. Why? No Formalities.

Well, you didn't have to dress to go to the club. You didn't have to wear your best clothes. You didn't have to sit over a table and look bored. On that night you received you in shirt-sleeves and you felt right at home. And you weren't bored. No, for here was the place where you could meet the people you wanted to meet. The artists, the writers, the actors, the musicians—all came to the Jockey Club.

No Formality at the Jockey. The place became known all over the world. "Certainly the most pleasant night-club of Europe," wrote the swanky New Yorker.

It was at the Jockey that Marlene Dietrich first met Josef von Sternberg and later rose to stardom. Who were just a few of the other guests? One could name them endlessly, but just for a few: Charlie Chaplin, Ferenc Molnar, famous dramatist, George Bancroft, movie star, Luigi Pirandello, famous Italian writer and recent Nobel Prize Winner, Alexander Kupter, George Gross, Irwin Piconne—internationally known artists, Eric Remarque, author of "All Quiet on the Western Front", Thomas Mann, Klaus Mann, Ernest Toller—all famous authors. Max Reinhardt—stage producer.

Nazis Ended Club
After the advent of the Third Reich, the Jockey Club became Chez Fredy in Paris, and later came back to Berlin. But the Nazis made life miserable for the night clubs. Spies were posted everywhere: it was impossible for people to meet in clubs to discuss the most innocuous subjects. Many of Fredy's friends disappeared.

And a month ago with Jack, bartender known from Downing Street eastward to Fifth Avenue, Mr. H. Wendt, actor, artist, photographer, and Mr. B. B. Baruch, journalist, critic, writer, Fredy left Germany for good and arrived in Shanghai Saturday on the Conte Rosso.

"I don't intend to establish just another night-club here," the genial maestro told a CHINA PRESS reporter yesterday. "The club I want to establish isn't here. It never has been here. It will have spontaneity, informality, lightness, gaiety—it will be almost like a private club where people can meet each other and be glad of it—and not bored. They will discuss art, music, literature, Chinese culture, those who are artists will lend their talent: in short, it will be a real gathering place where people are alive and not slumped over a whiskey soda.

"I have a feeling that there is a real need for such a club in Shanghai, especially for the young people who have ideas, life, youth, and vitality. The club will be a place where anybody can drop in, will be welcomed, and will join in the spirit of the club. Well, it's awfully hard to put it in words, but when it is started, and I hope it will be soon, you can best see by actually being there. I think Shanghai has great possibilities, and I hope I am right."

(批：Roy Please file 16 MAY 1935)

《字林西报》，1935年3月14日，星期四
S. B. 登记处。
6-7-8
930—柏林—玛琳邂逅冯·斯登堡

在1930年1月之前，玛琳·黛德丽（Marlene Dietrich）的名字几乎无人知晓。但在弗雷迪·考夫曼（Fredy Kauffmann）的乔基俱乐部（Jockey Club）的一个晚上，这位导演和这位明星首次相遇，因为在乔基俱乐部，这类事情总是会发生。上图拍摄于他们相遇的那晚。左侧是考夫曼先生，冯·斯登堡导演正躲在那匹纸马后面，椅子上坐着著名的德国电影导演古斯塔夫·弗罗利希（Gustav Froelich），右侧则是美丽的玛琳。考夫曼先生目前身在上海，希望在此创办一家“乔基俱乐部”。

柏林著名乔基俱乐部的 maestro（大师/经营者）
在此有计画

新近抵沪的弗雷迪·考夫曼认为上海需要
真正的夜总会；宣称该市的夜生活
令人厌烦、沉闷、难以忍受

厌倦。
据弗雷迪·考夫曼先生称，这种难以忍受的、彻底的、低俗的、慵懒的、沉闷的、死气沉沉的、毫无色彩的、宿命论般的厌倦，是上海夜生活的“特色”。考夫曼先生曾是柏林这一夜生活中心的著名乔基俱乐部的 maestro（大师/经营者）。

但据弗雷迪说（因为他不喜欢被称为“先生”），上海人并不想感到厌倦。如果给他们一个真正的俱乐部，一种真正的氛围，一种没有当代夜生活那种呆板拘谨的氛围，如果他们一旦领略到真正的自发性，那么——情况就会不同。而弗雷迪正致力于建立这样一家俱乐部。

但弗雷迪是谁？他是一位白发苍苍、和蔼可亲的中年德国人，是各地艺术家、女演员、名流、作家的朋友。这一切都发生在1929年，或者确切地说是在那之前。在此之前，弗雷迪是一名摄影师，也是一名舞台和银幕演员。但在1929年，他看透了柏林夜生活的空虚。他创办了自己的俱乐部——乔基俱乐部——从大门首次敞开的那一刻起，它就取得了成功。为什么？因为没有繁文缛节。

嗯，去俱乐部不必盛装打扮。你不必穿上最好的衣服。你不必坐在桌旁摆出一副厌倦的样子。在那个夜晚，接待你的人穿着衬衫袖子，让你感觉宾至如归。而且你不会感到厌倦。不，因为在这里你可以遇到你想见的人。艺术家、作家、演员、音乐家——所有人都来到乔基俱乐部。

乔基俱乐部没有繁文缛节。这个地方闻名世界。“无疑是欧洲最宜人的夜总会，”时髦的《纽约客》杂志写道。

正是在乔基俱乐部，玛琳·黛德丽首次遇见了约瑟夫·冯·斯登堡（Josef von Sternberg），随后一举成名。其他客人还有谁？可以 endlessy（无休止地）列举下去，但仅举几例：查理·卓别林，著名剧作家费伦茨·莫尔纳（Ferenc Molnar），电影明星乔治·班克罗夫特（George Bancroft），著名意大利作家、近期诺贝尔奖得主路易吉·皮兰德娄（Luigi Pirandello），亚历山大·库普特（Alexander Kupter），乔治·格罗斯（George Gross），欧文·皮科恩（Irwin Piconne）——国际知名艺术家，《西线无战事》作者埃里希·雷马克（Eric Remarque），托马斯·曼，克劳斯·曼，恩斯特·托勒尔（Ernest Toller）——均为著名作家。马克斯·莱因哈特（Max Reinhardt）——舞台制作人。

纳粹终结了俱乐部
随着第三帝国的到来，乔基俱乐部变成了巴黎的“ Chez Fredy ”（弗雷迪之家），后来又回到了柏林。但纳粹让夜总会的日子变得痛苦不堪。到处都安插了间谍：人们不可能在俱乐部里聚会讨论即使是最无害的话题。弗雷迪的许多朋友失踪了。

一个月前，弗雷迪与调酒师杰克（Jack，其名声从唐宁街向东一直传到第五大道）、演员、艺术家、摄影师 H. 温特（H. Wendt）先生，以及记者、评论家、作家 B. B. 巴鲁赫（B. B. Baruch）先生一起，永远离开了德国，并于周六乘坐“罗索伯爵号”（Conte Rosso）抵达上海。

“我打算在这里建立的不仅仅又是一家夜总会，”这位和蔼的 maestro（大师/经营者）昨天告诉《字林西报》记者。“我想建立的俱乐部这里没有。这里从来就没有过。它将具有自发性、非正式性、轻松感和欢快感——它几乎像一个私人俱乐部，人们可以在那里彼此相见并为此感到高兴——而不是感到厌倦。他们将讨论艺术、音乐、文学、中国文化，那些艺术家将贡献他们的才华：简而言之，它将是一个真正的聚会场所，那里的人们充满活力，而不是瘫倒在威士忌苏打水旁。

“我感觉上海确实需要这样的俱乐部，特别是对于那些有思想、有生活、有青春和活力的年轻人来说。俱乐部将是一个任何人都可以顺道来访、受到欢迎并融入俱乐部精神的地方。嗯，这很难用语言描述，但当它开始营业时——我希望很快就能实现——你通过亲身到场才能最好地体会。我认为上海有很大的潜力，我希望我是对的。”

（批注：Roy 请于1935年5月16日归档）
